motion.name: entrance

motion.purpose: One orchestrated load moment; text rises and un-blurs without fading from zero.

narrative.overview:
A window-film workshop after dark. The page is tinted graphite, the product (glass) is the only translucent material on it, and the brand's logo red behaves as light: it glows behind the featured pane, rides the squeegee's edge, and fills the button that starts a WhatsApp chat. Everything that is not glass is solid, quiet and dark, so the one memorable moment (film sliding across a window, left to right) reads clearly.

Density is low and mobile-first. One family, Archivo, carries the whole hierarchy by changing width and weight: headings run wide and heavy like automotive lettering, body copy sits at normal width. Illustrations are fine chrome line drawings of a car, a house and a shopfront whose glass panes take real film fills (smoke, mirror, frost) and visibly hide the interior behind them. The system shows privacy instead of naming it.

The home keeps the flat vector glass selector; each service page (/autos, /hogares, /negocios) adds one scroll-driven 3D film scene in the same world: a dark photo studio, graphite bodies whose curves draw chrome reflections, warm interiors seen through clear glass, and film applied pane by pane by a squeegee with a coral-to-white edge.
keyCharacteristics: Tinted blue-graphite ground, never flat black.
Red used only as light and action, never as decoration.
Real glassmorphism (backdrop blur) only on the three hero panes, because they are windows.
One variable typeface, hierarchy by width axis (100 to 125) and weight (400 to 820).
Pill controls, softly rounded solid cards, hairline edges at 14% ink.
One signature motion: a squeegee applying film, driven by a single CSS number (`--film`, 0 to 1).
One scroll-driven 3D film scene per service page (Three.js, rendered on demand): the film is applied while the visitor scrolls.

rules.name: The Red Is Light Rule
rules.body: Red appears only where light or action is: the backlight under the featured pane, CTA fills and their glow, the squeegee edge, the active-nav underline, the focus ring and text selection. Icons, headings, borders and ornaments stay in ink.

rules.name: The Clear Glass Rule
rules.body: Unfilmed glass is always lighter than its surroundings and shows the interior behind it; a film must visibly darken, mirror or frost that view. If a film does not change what is seen through the glass, it is not reading as film.

rules.name: The Graphite Not Black Rule
rules.body: Page and surface backgrounds are blue graphite (#0c0f13, #1a1e24). Near-black values exist only as materials inside the drawings (tire, smoke film).

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the only typeface. Hierarchy comes from the width axis and weight, never from a second family or a system display face.

rules.name: The Fit-To-Word Rule
rules.body: The display word scales to its own length and to the viewport height (`--title-chars`), so the longest service name never clips and the shortest never floats small.

rules.name: The Glass Only Where Glass Is Rule
rules.body: `backdrop-filter` blur (16px, saturate 1.3) exists only on the three hero panes, because they are windows. Cards, menus and sections are solid.

rules.name: The Light Behind Glass Rule
rules.body: The featured pane is lit from behind: a red radial glow shares its grid cell and sits under it, and the pane's own blur diffuses it. Red light is placed behind glass, not painted on it.

rules.name: The Film Scene Rule
rules.body: 3D objects are graphite (paint #353d47, walls #323841) lit by strip-softbox reflections, with a low red rim only in the car studio. Glass starts clear with a warm interior visible behind it; the film must change what is seen. No pedestals, lawns, trees, props or realistic stock models. One scene per page, rendered only when scroll or size changes.

dos: Do take every color, radius, easing and film fill from the custom properties in `src/styles/tokens.css`; add new values there first.
Do use pills (999px) for every control, 14px for solid surfaces, and 20px only for glass frames.
Do draw new illustrations as chrome line art over filled body shapes, with the interior visible through clear glass, so a dark film has something to hide.
Do drive any film animation through the single `--film` number (0 to 1) and let CSS transitions interpolate it; script only changes state attributes.
Do ease with `--ease-out` (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for movement and `--ease-in-out` (cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)) for peeling and toggles; keep state changes at 0.2–0.25s.

Do honor `prefers-reduced-motion`: drop transitions and the entrance. With motion on, the hero headline, lede and actions stay visible from the first frame: their entrance rises and un-blurs them but never fades them in from zero.
Do give every new 3D film pane its own progress window and keep camera keyframes on the chapter beats (0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1).
donts: Don't put `backdrop-filter` glass on cards, menus or sections; translucent blur is reserved for the hero panes.
Don't use red on icons, headings, borders or decorative accents; red is light and action only.
Don't use pure black or flat neutral grey for page or surface backgrounds.
Don't add a second typeface or a system display face.
Don't put 3D anywhere but the service-page film scene, and never with pedestals, lawns, low-poly props, silver showroom paint or realistic stock models (see The Film Scene Rule).
Don't replace the illustrations with stock or placeholder photos; only real job photos, through the service's `photo` field, replace the art.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, top, margin); motion uses transform, opacity, filter and `--film`.
